'''King:''' {{legend0|#A5B0FF|40–50%}} | title = [[Governor of Utah|Governor]] | before_election = [[Spencer Cox]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Spencer Cox]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{Elections in Utah}} The '''2024 Utah gubernatorial election''' was held on November 5, 2024, to elect the [[List of governors of Utah|governor of Utah]]. Incumbent Governor [[Spencer Cox]] ran for a second term, winning the Republican primary against state representative [[Phil Lyman]] with 54.4% of the vote; Lyman later mounted a write-in campaign for the general election. Cox won the general election in November, defeating Democratic nominee and state representative [[Brian King (politician)|Brian King]] as well as Lyman.{{cite news |title=Utah Governor Election Results 2024: Cox vs. Smith King |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2024/11/05/us/elections/results-utah-governor.html |access-date=November 7, 2024 |work=The New York Times |date=November 5, 2024}} This was the worst performance for a Republican gubernatorial candidate since [[1992 Utah gubernatorial election|1992]], which also saw a major independent candidate. Cox's 24.43% margin of victory was also the smallest since [[2004 Utah gubernatorial election|2004]]. Democrats have not won a gubernatorial election in Utah since [[1980 Utah gubernatorial election|1980]]. == Background == Utah is considered to be a strongly [[Red states and blue states|red state]] at the federal and state levels: Republicans control all statewide executive offices, the entire congressional delegation, and supermajorities in both state legislative chambers. In the [[2020 United States presidential election in Utah|2020 presidential election]], [[Donald Trump]] carried Utah by 20.5%.{{Cite web |title=Party control of Utah state government |url=https://ballotpedia.org/Party_control_of_Utah_state_government |access-date=2023-03-19 |website=Ballotpedia |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Utah 2020 presidential election results |url=https://www.cnn.com/election/2020/results/state/utah/president |access-date=2023-03-19 |website=www.cnn.com |language=en}} Cox was first elected in [[2020 Utah gubernatorial election|2020]], defeating Christopher Peterson by 32.65%.{{Cite web |title=Utah 2020 gubernatorial results |url=https://www.cnn.com/election/2020/results/state/utah/governor |access-date=2023-03-19 |website=www.cnn.com |language=en}} ==Republican primary== Incumbent Republican governor [[Spencer Cox (politician)|Spencer Cox]] faced criticism from many conservatives for his moderate political positions, including his veto of HB11,{{cite news |work=[[Politico]] |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2022/03/22/utah-governor-veto-transgender-sports-ban-00019417 |date=March 22, 2022 |title=Utah governor becomes latest to veto transgender sports ban}} and opposition to former president [[Donald Trump]].{{cite news |access-date=June 24, 2024 |author=Samuel Benson |work=Deseret News |url=https://www.deseret.com/2024/2/15/24074164/utah-gov-cox-republicans-making-a-huge-mistake-if-they-nominate-trump/ |date=February 15, 2024 |title=Utah Gov. Cox: Republicans making 'a huge mistake' if they nominate Trump}} Cox was booed at the Utah Republican state convention in April 2024.{{cite news |access-date=June 24, 2024 |author=Hannah Schoenbaum |work=AP News |url=https://apnews.com/article/utah-republican-governor-debate-cox-lyman-c0844d83cb07d02d8638b4b12dcbec99 |date=June 12, 2024 |title=Utah governor defends record in primary debate after harsh reception at GOP convention}} He faced a primary challenge from state representative [[Phil Lyman]], who won over 67% of the vote at the convention.{{cite news |access-date=June 24, 2024 |author=Brigham Tomco |work=Deseret News |url=https://www.deseret.com/utah/2024/04/27/utah-gop-governor-convention-results/ |date=April 27, 2024 |title=Phil Lyman beats Gov. Spencer Cox at Utah GOP convention. Both advance to primary}} However, Cox collected enough signatures to appear on the primary ballot. Cox consistently led Lyman in polls and won re-nomination, though Lyman refused to concede.{{cite news |author=Bridger Beal-Cvetko |date=June 25, 2024 |title=Spencer Cox cruises to win in GOP primary; Phil Lyman says he won't concede |url=https://www.ksl.com/article/51052654/spencer-cox-cruises-to-win-in-gop-primary-phil-lyman-says-he-wont-concede |work=[[Deseret News]]}}{{cite news |author=Katie McKellar |date=June 25, 2024 |title=AP calls race for Utah Gov. Spencer Cox, but Lyman won't concede |url=https://utahnewsdispatch.com/2024/06/25/race-utah-governor-cox-leads-lyman-republican-primary-election-night-results/ |work=Utah News Dispatch}} ===Candidates=== ====Nominee==== *[[Spencer Cox (politician)|Spencer Cox]], incumbent governor{{cite news |title=Are Utah Republicans mad at Gov. The [[Utah Supreme Court]] rejected his argument.{{Cite news |last=Gehrke |first=Robert |date=August 13, 2024 |title=Utah Supreme Court rejects Phil Lyman's bid to kick Gov. Spencer Cox off the ballot and out of office |url=https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2024/08/13/spencer-cox-will-stay-ballot/ |access-date=August 15, 2024 |work=Salt Lake Tribune}} Lyman later announced that he would run as a write-in candidate.{{Cite news |last=Stern |first=Emily Anderson |date=August 12, 2024 |title=After losing GOP primary, Phil Lyman will run as a write-in candidate for Utah governor |url=https://www.sltrib.com/news/politics/2024/08/12/phil-lyman-will-mount-write-in-bid/ |access-date=August 15, 2024 |work=Salt Lake Tribune}} Cox has since backed Trump after an [[Attempted assassination of Donald Trump in Pennsylvania|assassination attempt]] made during a rally in Pennsylvania on July 13, stating in a letter: "Your life was spared. Now, because of that miracle, you have the opportunity to do something that no other person on earth can do right now: unify and save our country."{{Cite web |last=Sullivan |first=Kate |date=2024-07-19 |title=Utah Republican Gov. Spencer Cox pledges Trump his support after saying last week he wouldn't vote for him |url=https://www.cnn.com/2024/07/19/politics/utah-gov-spencer-cox-trump-support/index.html |access-date=2024-08-12 |website=CNN |language=en}} Cox also stated in a later news conference: “I am doing everything I can to help and support him...We will still have lots of disagreements, I’m sure, and we’ll still do everything we can to help the state of Utah and help the Republican Party be successful.”{{Cite web |last=Sentner |first=Irie |date=July 19, 2024 |title=Utah governor, a longtime Trump skeptic, offers endorsement after assassination attempt |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2024/07/19/utah-governor-spencer-cox-endorses-trump-00169793 |access-date=August 11, 2024 |website=Politico}} ==Democratic primary== ===Candidates=== ====Nominee==== * [[Brian King (politician)|Brian King]], [[Utah House of Representatives|state representative]] from the 23rd district (2009–present) and former Minority Leader of the Utah House of Representatives (2015–2023){{cite news |work=[[Axios (website)|Axios]] |access-date=January 5, 2024 |date=December 4, 2023 |title=State Rep.
